title: Nonlinear collective dynamics and microwave comb generation in a diamond maser
authors: Christoph W. Zollitsch, Jonas N. Bach, Christopher W. M. Kay, Jonathan D. Breeze
abstract: Optically pumped room temperature masers are a promising platform for driven dissipative spin photon physics beyond steady state emission. Here we observe a sequence of dynamical thresholds in a room temperature nitrogen vacancy diamond maser as the optical pump is increased above the conventional masing threshold. The first threshold yields narrow-line continuous wave emission, while a second threshold produces a periodic train of microwave pulses whose repetition rate generates a frequency comb spectrum. At higher pump power, a third threshold gives rise to pulses with an oscillatory, frequency chirped decay. Time-resolved measurements link the comb directly to self-pulsing dynamics and Fourier analysis of individual bursts reveals a broad distribution of frequencies consistent with collective spin-resonator dynamics in an inhomogeneously broadened ensemble. These results establish the diamond maser as a room temperature platform for nonlinear nonequilibrium light matter dynamics and microwave comb generation.
summary: This paper reports on observing multiple nonlinear dynamical thresholds in a room-temperature diamond maser utilizing $	ext{NV}^-$ centers. As the optical pump power increases, the maser transitions from continuous wave emission to a periodic train of microwave pulses, generating a frequency comb. The analysis confirms that these dynamics are governed by nonlinear collective spin-resonator interactions.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonlinear collective dynamics and the generation of microwave frequency combs within a room-temperature maser system.
main_result: The maser exhibits three distinct nonlinear thresholds as the pump rate increases, leading to the generation of a frequency comb spectrum from periodic microwave pulses.
method: The research employs time-resolved measurements of output power, Fourier analysis (FFT) of transient signals, and spectroscopy across different pump rates.
model_or_system: The system is an optically pumped nitrogen-vacancy ($	ext{NV}^-$) center ensemble in diamond, operating as a maser coupled to a high-quality factor microwave resonator.
key_observables: Output power ($P_{out}$), linewidths ($\sigma, \Gamma$), comb teeth spacing ($\sim 3.8 	ext{ kHz}$), and transient pulse shapes.
important_parameters: Three distinct nonlinear thresholds; resonator $Q$-factor of $\sim 42,772$; pulse period $T \approx 261 \mu	ext{s}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the maser dynamics are governed by nonlinear collective spin-resonator interactions, and the linewidths are compared against the inhomogeneous broadening.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition from CW emission to periodic pulsing (comb) and the subsequent oscillatory, chirped decay, confirmed by time-domain transients and FFT spectra.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the three spectral regimes via power measurements, then using time-resolved spectroscopy to confirm the periodic pulsing, and finally using FFT analysis to characterize the frequency content and chirp of the pulses.
why_interesting: This work provides a clean, solid-state platform for observing driven, dissipative, nonlinear dynamics, particularly the transition to coherent, structured light emission (frequency combs) in a solid-state quantum emitter system.

Partially Pumped Collective Emitters.note: The observation of nonlinear thresholds and frequency comb generation in a collective maser system directly relates to the physics of collective emission dynamics, particularly the transition from continuous to pulsed/structured emission driven by pump rate.
